initial-state.t: K-Means alternates assignment and update. We track the **objective**: the sum of squared distances from every point to its assigned center (**WCSS**). Smaller means tighter clusters.

assignment-1.t: Assign each customer to its nearest center. With these starting centers the **WCSS is 82.06**.

update-1.t: Move each center to the mean of its group. With the same memberships, the **WCSS falls to 13.06**.

objective-drops.t: From **82.06 to 13.06** just by moving the centers. The update step **cannot make the objective larger**, because the mean is the best center for a fixed group.

assignment-2.t: With the moved centers, the stray customer at **(6.8, 6.8)** switches to the middle cluster. Reassigning to nearer centers cannot raise the objective: it is now **6.31**.

update-2.t: Move the centers to the new group means: **(1.68, 2.0), (6.58, 6.12) and (3.67, 8.28)**. The WCSS is **4.18**.

objective-drops-again.t: **6.31 to 4.18.** Every step either lowers the objective or leaves it unchanged, so K-Means cannot wander.

stable-centers.t: A third assignment changes **no memberships**, so a third update would not move the centers. The WCSS stays at **4.18**.

converged.t: Memberships and centers are stable: K-Means has **converged** after two updates. Convergence is guaranteed to happen in a finite number of rounds.

different-initialization-preview.t: Convergence is **not** the global best. From the starting centers (1, 2), (2, 2) and (5, 7) the loop also converges, but to a **worse solution (WCSS 29.48)**: one natural group is split and two are merged.
